title: Veil and Hollow Revisited
premise: Paloma Delacroix, a runaway apprentice hiding her hedge-witch gift in the smuggler's warrens of the Thornfell mountains, learns that the crown's gift-hunt is being fed by informants from the Hollow, the fae realm her old mistress once served. When her mistress is taken and Paloma's own name surfaces on the hunt lists, she must gather a found family of outcasts—a disgraced huntsman, a half-fae child, and a smuggler who owes her his life—and cross into the Hollow to reforge the covenant that once kept both realms at peace. The hunt's true architect is the crown's spymaster, himself secretly gifted and determined to destroy the covenant so no one will ever hold power he cannot control. In the climactic confrontation beneath the winter-dark Thornfell, Paloma binds the covenant to her own blood rather than to any crown, ending the hunt but exiling herself from the Hollow forever; she returns to find her found family waiting, and together they begin building a new, unregistered kind of magic in the mountains.
about_author: Gideon Fairweather is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fantasy. They write stories about borders—geographic, magical, and personal—from a small stone cottage they insist is not haunted.

chapters.title: Salt on the Mountain Road
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She runs contraband herbs and charms along the smuggler roads, keeping her gift buried, until she heals a stranger's fever with an involuntary touch and realizes someone saw. The chapter establishes her competence, her loneliness, and her rule of invisibility. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of being witnessed for the first time in six years.

chapters.title: The Crown's Long Winter
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Proclamation posters appear in every village: all gifted persons to be registered, hunted, or burned. Paloma races to warn her old mistress, Maren, only to find the cottage ransacked and Maren gone, a black iron sigil of the crown's spymaster left behind. Emotional beat: grief curdling into guilt—she was supposed to protect her teacher by staying away.

chapters.title: A Smuggler's Debt
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She calls in a debt from Corvin, a smuggler whose life she once saved, and gains passage and shelter. Corvin's crew includes Wren, a half-fae child the crew protects without understanding why. Paloma recognizes Wren's gift and must choose whether to expose herself by teaching the girl control. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness; the first crack in her isolation.

chapters.title: The Huntsman Who Laid Down His Bow
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Dain, a royal huntsman who faked his own death rather than hunt the gifted. He tracks Paloma not to capture her but to warn her: the hunt's informant lists come from the Hollow itself, and the spymaster, Lord Cassel, is gathering gifted prisoners for something worse than execution. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people trained to distrust.

chapters.title: What Maren Buried Under the Rowan
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following Maren's hidden notes, Paloma learns of the old covenant between Thornfell and the Hollow, sealed in blood and broken a generation ago—the break that made the fae informants and the crown's fear possible. The notes reveal Maren was the covenant's last living keeper. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering her whole life was shaped by a war she never knew existed.

chapters.title: The Hollow's Toll
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The group crosses into the Hollow through a smuggler's gate only the fae-blooded can open. Wren, half of both worlds, experiences the Hollow as home and threat at once, while the fae court offers Paloma Maren's freedom in exchange for the covenant's blood-price—Paloma's own. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging offered at an unbearable price.

chapters.title: Cassel's Confession
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Captured and brought before Lord Cassel, Dain discovers the spymaster is himself gifted, hiding in plain sight, and destroying the covenant so that magic will exist only as the crown's secret weapon. Cassel offers Dain his old life back if he betrays Paloma's route into the Hollow. Emotional beat: Dain's crisis of loyalty—truth versus the comfort of rejoining the world that made him.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Cassel's forces seal the gates; the Hollow begins dying of the same unnatural winter gripping Thornfell, and Maren, dying in her cell, tells Paloma the covenant was never meant to bind the fae—it was meant to bind the keeper. Paloma accepts the blood-price, but on her own terms: she will carry the covenant alone, exiled from both realms. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely, grief and resolve fused.

chapters.title: Veilfire
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, climax. In the frozen heart of the Hollow, Paloma reforges the covenant with her own blood while Cassel's hunters breach the veil behind her. Corvin, Wren, and Dain hold the gate—each choosing the found family over survival. The covenant flares, the winter breaks, and Cassel's stolen gift is stripped from him as the magic passes beyond any crown's reach. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into triumph, at real cost.

chapters.title: Hollow and Home
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, resolution. Exiled from the Hollow but no longer hunted, Paloma returns to Thornfell, where Maren—freed but frail—and the others have begun teaching unregistered, covenant-born magic to mountain folk. Paloma plants a rowan on Maren's rebuilt cottage and finally stops running. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won belonging; inheritance remade as choice rather than burden.
